unreleased: The repository module now stores records: each has a name and a slug of its own (the slug is made from the name, editable and unique in the table) and a value for any of the table's attributes, checked on the server with a short error code per attribute (text, number, true/false, date, date and time, an image, a reference to a record of the same repository, and lists and maps of one simple type, a list being renumbered whenever its order changes). Records are deleted softly and can be restored, and deleted for good only once deleted and only while no other record refers to them. They are listed a page at a time (25, 50 or 100) with filters by every attribute that has an operator for it (text contains / equals, number comparisons and ranges, dates before / after / between, a chosen record, empty / not empty), a quick search, sorting by any column with empty values last, and a switch for deleted records; a picker endpoint searches a table for a reference. Images (png, jpeg, webp or gif, recognised by their content, never SVG) are uploaded or imported from an address and stored in the database as base64: the server refuses to download from internal addresses (loopback, private, link-local, metadata, redirects included), uploads nobody claims are deleted after a day, and a person's images are limited in size and in total

Add a repository module (app/modules/repository): everyone who is signed in creates their own repositories (databases) with tables whose attributes they define themselves - text, number, boolean, date, date and time, image, a reference to a record of another table of the same repository, and a list or map of one simple type. Everything is private to its owner (somebody else's data answers 404), slugs are made from names and checked live, limits per user live in backend/modules/repository.json, a table's attributes are saved as one ordered list (the type of a saved attribute never changes, and removing one that records hold values for asks for confirmation first), and a repository or table is deleted by confirming its name. Records, images, filters and statistics follow
